title: NTSOne: Registrations, ID cards and tickets

scenes.card: Registrations, ID cards and tickets|Run a registration from start to finish
scenes.text: In this video you will learn how to run a registration from start to finish with NTSOne. Create a program, build and publish its form, collect registrations, and manage them.

scenes.title: 1. Create a program
scenes.text: Open Programs and choose New Program. Give it a name and a short description, then select Create program. Your program starts as a draft, with tabs for its form, registrations, analytics and verifications.

scenes.title: 2. Build the form
scenes.text: Next, open the Form Builder. Choose a type of question, such as Short Text, press Add field, and give it a label. You can mark a question as required. There are twenty three question types to choose from.

scenes.title: 3. Add your questions and preview
scenes.text: Add the rest of your questions: email, phone number, date of birth, or a yes or no question. Use Preview to see exactly how the form will look to the people who register.

scenes.title: 4. Publish and share
scenes.text: When you are happy with it, choose Save Draft, then Publish. Then publish the program itself and open registration. Your program now has a public link and a QR code that you can share.

scenes.title: 5. What registrants see
scenes.text: This is what a registrant sees. If they miss a required answer, the problem is shown right under that question, with a red outline, so they know exactly what to fix.

scenes.title: 6. Submitting
scenes.text: As they fill in the form, each answer turns green when it is correct. After they submit, they receive a registration number, and they can preview, print or download a copy of their registration.

scenes.title: 7. Manage registrations
scenes.text: Back in your workspace, the Registrations tab lists everyone who has registered. You can search, filter by status or date, import from Excel, and export to Excel or CSV. Open a registration to read every answer.

scenes.title: 8. Update a status
scenes.text: To update a registration, choose a new status, such as Approved, add an optional note, and press Update status. Every change is saved in the history.

scenes.title: 9. ID cards, tickets and check-in
scenes.text: NTSOne can also issue ID cards and tickets with a QR code. Turn them on from the program page, pick a design, and each registrant gets their own. When a code is scanned at the door, the Verifications tab records who it was, whether it was valid, and when.
That is how you run a registration with NTSOne. Use this video as your guide, and watch the next video to learn about voting polls.
